scope: This is a read-only, incremental check of public sources for priority and applicability of the unaccepted conditional Olson-lane candidate G-LS. It does not judge correctness. No computation, file writes, git actions, model CLI calls, paid APIs or outside contact were made. It reuses parent note v4 and scout v5, so SC/DGM/index-one and the Lev Theorem 2 statement were not re-surveyed. Source theorems are kept separate from my own deductions, and every deduction is marked [INFERENCE]. No audit timestamp is given: this agent can only read files, so it cannot run /bin/date.
summary: The bounded screen found no published or preprint statement that contains G-LS, the full original LS(p,κ) (p≥5, 0≤κ≤p−2), or a stronger statement implying either. Not finding one does not show that G-LS is new or that LS is open.

[INFERENCE] Standard form. Since C_(2p)≅C_2×C_p, LS is a statement about even-length zero-sum subsequences of a C_p-sequence, with the even lengths in [2κ+2,2p] excluded. Applying EGZ twice in C_p shows that (ZP_κ) forces |Y|≤3p−2. So G-LS only concerns lengths 3p−2e+1≤|Y|≤3p−2, where e=p−κ.

[INFERENCE] That length cap means the classical structure theorems for n-zero-free sequences with n=2p never apply on the LS domain: Savchev–Chen needs length >3n/2−1, Gao–Li–Yuan–Zhuang Cor. 9 needs length ≥3p, and inverse EGZ is at length 4p−2. The length-set invariants (s_L, s_dN, η, s_≤k, E_k, disc, disc_ℓ, and the Fan et al. property) only guarantee that some zero-sum exists, or deal with short or single lengths. None of them implies the conditional statement LS.

New since scout v5; this concerns where the external import comes from and is not an LS antecedent. Zeng–Yuan (EJC 2023) quotes Gao–Peng–Wang (JCTA 2011): a sequence with no zero-sum of length ≤h(S) and |Σ(S)|<min{|G|,2|S|−1} is strictly behaving. [INFERENCE] Applying this inside ⟨supp S⟩ gives exactly the Lev Theorem 2 normal form that G-LS imports. Lev v3 does not cite Gao–Peng–Wang. I did not read the Gao–Peng–Wang paper itself.

Ordered Olson: I found no public result settling it, either for D_(2p) or for finite groups in general. A 2025 arXiv paper still poses a stronger ordered-EGZ statement as a conjecture, and all dihedral and metacyclic EGZ results found from 2022–2026 are unordered. STAB and LS+: I found no public result settling either.

If G-LS were accepted, it would be a modest specialist extension. It is not a routine corollary of any theorem I found, and it is not shown to be consequential. It uses the same mechanism as the accepted BASE2 cells. On its own, or combined with S1-sharp, it gives neither INV* nor ordered Olson.

local_targets.G_LS: Hypotheses: p≥7 prime, floor(2p/3)+1≤κ≤p−2, Y an odd sequence over C_(2p) with |Y|≥p+2κ+1 and no zero-sum occurrence subsequence of length in [2κ+2,2p]. Conclusion: every zero-sum subsequence has length ≤2κ. Source: proof §0. Status: unaccepted, conditional on Lev Theorem 2.
local_targets.original_LS: Same implication for p≥5 and 0≤κ≤p−2 (LS-scope-v1.md lines 10-12).
local_targets.accepted_S1_sharp: Same implication with no bound on |Y|, for 0≤κ≤floor(2p/3). The verdict says it fails at every κ in [floor(2p/3)+1,p], shown by the explicit F1 family (verdict lines 5-9).

standard_translation_INFERENCE: For odd p, the map x↦(x mod 2, x mod p) gives C_(2p)≅C_2×C_p. The odd residues form the coset {1}×C_p and correspond one-to-one with C_p. Let S=(y mod p) be the image of Y in C_p. A subsequence of Y sums to zero exactly when it has even length and its image sums to zero in C_p.
LS(p,κ) is equivalent to: if a C_p-sequence S with |S|≥p+2κ+1 has no even-length zero-sum subsequence with length in [2κ+2,2p], then it has no even-length zero-sum subsequence of length ≥2κ+2.
Contrapositive: if an odd Y with |Y|≥p+2κ+1 has a zero-sum of length ≥2p+2, then it has a zero-sum with length in [2κ+2,2p]. That second zero-sum may use terms outside the long one.

Length cap: any 3p−1 terms of C_p contain two disjoint p-term zero-sums (EGZ twice), so they contain a 2p-term zero-sum. For odd terms this is a zero-sum in C_(2p), and 2p lies in the excluded interval whenever κ≤p−1. So (ZP_κ) forces |Y|≤3p−2, and G-LS covers 3p−2e+1≤|Y|≤3p−2. When e=2 only |Y|∈{3p−3,3p−2} remain. The RED import in the proof reduces any counterexample to |Y|=3p−2e+1.

S1-sharp at κ is equivalent to: every odd zero-sum sequence of length ≥2p+2 contains a zero-sum subsequence with length in [2κ+2,2p] (take Y=T). Above floor(2p/3) the F1 family rules out this form, so G-LS has to use the extra length.

candidates.source_statement: Characterizes the n-zero-free sequences in Z_n (no zero-sum of length n) of length >3n/2−1. The authors say the characterization cannot be extended in the same form to shorter lengths.
candidates.group_and_lengths: Z_n with n=2p, any residues; applies to |S|≥3p.
candidates.restriction_direction: Excludes only length 2p. G-LS excludes every even length in [2κ+2,2p], which includes 2p.
candidates.comparison: [INFERENCE] By the length cap, no odd sequence satisfying (ZP_κ) has length ≥3p−1. The two length ranges do not overlap.

candidates.source_statement: Cor. 9: an n-zero-sum free S over Z_n with |S|=n+ℓ, where ℓ≥n/p′+p′−2 and p′ is the least prime dividing n, satisfies g+S=0^h·T·S′ with h≥ℓ+1, T zero-sum and S′ zero-sum free. Thm 3 (odd n≥50): zero-sum free sequences with length in (n/3+1, n/2] have index ≤1−4/n after deleting at most two terms.
candidates.group_and_lengths: For n=2p, p′=2, so Cor. 9 needs |S|≥3p.
candidates.restriction_direction: Cor. 9 excludes only length n. Thm 3 concerns zero-sum free sequences and says nothing about length intervals.
candidates.comparison: [INFERENCE] Cor. 9 never applies on the LS domain because of the cap. Thm 3 is a structure result for zero-sum free sequences. It is weaker than Lev's normal form and relies on cited unpublished manuscripts.

candidates.source_statement: For a solvable group of order n, a (2n−2)-multiset with no n-term product equal to 1 forces the group to be cyclic, with two values each repeated n−1 times. The product order is chosen.
Title only: 'On the structure of n-zero-sum free sequences over cyclic groups of order n', IJNT 10(08) (2014) 1991–2009. The abstract could not be accessed.
candidates.comparison: [INFERENCE] Suppose a characterization holds only for |S|≥3p−c. It reaches the G-LS threshold 3p−2e+1 only when e≤(c+1)/2, while e goes up to p−floor(2p/3)−1, about p/3. It could cover a few fixed-e cells, such as the already accepted e=2 cells, but not the whole domain unless it works down to about 7p/3 and controls the whole excluded interval.

candidates.id: length-set invariants (ZZ21 s_L, Theorem A s_dN, Schmid01 E_k, Zhao25 s_≤k, GLZZ16 disc_ℓ, HL25 disc, FGWZZ11)
candidates.source_statement: s_L(G) is the least ℓ forcing a zero-sum with length in L. s_dN(C_n)=lcm(n,d)+gcd(n,d)−1. E_k asks for a zero-sum with k∤|T|, defined only when k∤exp G. s_≤k is defined for k∈[exp G, D(G)−1]. disc_ℓ asks for a zero-sum of length ≠ℓ; disc asks for two zero-sums of different lengths. FGWZZ11: in non-cyclic G, zero-sum sequences of length exactly t∈[exp+1, η−1] contain a zero-sum of length in [1, exp G].
candidates.restriction_direction: Each one guarantees that some zero-sum exists, or concerns short or single lengths.
candidates.comparison: [INFERENCE] LS is a conditional statement about sequences whose zero-sums may all be short, so no value of s_L, even for L=[2κ+2,2p] and odd sequences only, gives it. s_2N(C_p)=2p only guarantees some even-length zero-sum. E_2 is undefined for C_(2p) and looks for odd lengths in C_p. s_≤k has no admissible k in cyclic groups. FGWZZ11's range of t is empty for cyclic groups, because η(C_n)=n.

candidates.id: few-subsum normal forms (L22; GPW11 as quoted in ZY23; ZY23 Thm 4 / Cor. 5)
candidates.source_statement: L22 Thm 2 (read by the parent): if α is zero-sum-free of length n with |Σ_inc(α)|<2n, then α=(x_i a) with 1=x_1≤…≤x_n, x_(j+1)≤x_1+…+x_j, Σ_inc={0,a,…,Sa} and S<ord(a). GPW11 as quoted in ZY23: if ⟨supp S⟩=G and S has no zero-sum of length ≤h(S), then S is strictly g-behaving or |Σ(S)|≥min{|G|,2|S|−1}. ZY23 gives an explicit list at |Σ(S)|=2|S|−1.
candidates.restriction_direction: Zero-sum-free sequences, or no short zero-sums. No length intervals.
candidates.comparison: These are inputs to G-LS §0, not LS-level statements. [INFERENCE] Take S zero-sum-free and H=⟨supp S⟩. Then |Σ(S)|≤2|S|−2<min{|H|,2|S|−1}, so GPW gives strictly behaving, with Σn_i<ord(g) (otherwise ord(g)·g∈Σ(S)). That is exactly Lev's conclusion, with no half-order length hypothesis. The G-LS §0 transcription matches scout v5's (no '+1', inclusive Σ). ZY23's boundary case |Σ_inc|=2n is not needed, because G-LS uses a strict bound.
These concern zero-sums of length ≤h(S) or the length of the shortest zero-sum. That is the opposite end of the length range from LS's interval [2κ+2,2p].

candidates.id: nonabelian EGZ (ZW26, ORZZ25, ABR22, OZ20, GGOZ; YP84)
candidates.comparison: All are unordered: the product may be taken 'in some order'. None preserves the original order, and none bears on the abelian LS lemma.

candidates.comparison: Not read: no abstract or full text was available, as already noted in scout v5. Nothing is inferred from the title.

counterevidence_and_nuance: I found no source that states LS or poses it as a problem. I also found no contrary result, such as a published counterexample family above floor(2p/3) at length ≥p+2κ+1.
GPW11, as quoted, would be an earlier journal source for the normal form G-LS imports. That lowers the novelty of the import step only, not of the LS conclusion.

Three items could not be read: PQSW14, GZ05/06 and the JNT 2026 E_k paper. Some priority risk remains. For structure theorems on n-zero-free sequences, the [INFERENCE] length-cap argument limits that risk.

The e=2 cells sit at the top of the length cap, so an inverse theorem for 2p-zero-free C_p-sequences of length 3p−3 or 3p−2 could overlap them. Those cells are already accepted locally (LS-small) and are not the new content of G-LS.

G_LS_and_original_LS.result: No published equivalent or stronger statement located.
G_LS_and_original_LS.limit: Not finding one is not evidence of novelty or openness.

STAB.basis: STAB is a local name, and its definition was outside the authorized read set. I searched public sources for LS-type length-interval statements on odd C_(2p) sequences and for ordered or structural statements on D_(2p) words. I found only Olson's general conjecture and unordered EGZ results.
STAB.limit: Without the local definition I cannot check for an exact match.

LS_plus.basis: Same as STAB. The proof's §0 lists LS+ as a target distinct from G-LS.

ordered_Olson_D2p.identification_INFERENCE: The unrestricted local statement ('every length-(4p−1) word over D_2p has an identity 2p-subword in increasing index order') is Olson's conjecture as stated on OPG, taken at G=D_2p with n=2p.
ordered_Olson_D2p.evidence: OPG says very little is known. GJM25a still poses the ordered constant as a conjecture. ZW26, ORZZ25, OZ20 and GGOZ are unordered, and ABR22 excludes s≡−1, the dihedral case.
ordered_Olson_D2p.limit: OPG is a 2007 page. Neither absence nor these sources prove the problem is open.

ordered_EGZ_general_finite_groups.evidence_INFERENCE: GJM25a Conj. 5.1 together with D_o(G)≤|G| (GJM26) would imply Olson's conjecture for every finite group. That conjecture is still open according to its own 2025 text.
ordered_EGZ_general_finite_groups.limit: This is a bounded screen, not a citation census.

Dimitrov_2004_baseline.source_attribution: GJM25a Thm 1.3 attributes D_o(G)≤L(G) for finite p-groups to Dimitrov, Math. Balkanica 18 (2004) 129–140 (their ref. [7]).
Dimitrov_2004_baseline.INFERENCE: Apply that bound to G×C_|G|, which is a p-group. Using L(G×C_n)=L(G)+n−1 (Jennings) and L(G)≤|G|, this gives ordered EGZ for p-groups, which matches the baseline you gave. D_(2p) with p odd is not a p-group, so the baseline does not cover it.

contribution_calibration.positive_characterization: A sequence-level lemma for odd sequences in C_(2p). Equivalently, it is about even-length zero-sums of C_p-sequences of length 3p−2e+1 to 3p−2 [INFERENCE]. It says that, given enough length, a long zero-sum forces one with length in [2κ+2,2p]. It covers the whole interval floor(2p/3)+1≤κ≤p−2 by extending the accepted two-cell BASE2 mechanism with a few-sums normal form.
contribution_calibration.why_not_routine_corollary: No theorem I found contains it. By the candidate's own outline it also needs candidate-specific steps: pinning the multiplier, locating Z0, two first-crossing bounds, a shortest-long-zero-sum witness lemma with variable j, and a signed-lift contradiction. These steps were not checked in this audit.
contribution_calibration.routine_or_existing_components: The CRT/parity translation and the length cap [INFERENCE]; the complement and interval arithmetic (scout v5); the AP lemmas. The normal form itself is an existing theorem: Lev 2022, and plausibly GPW 2011 [INFERENCE].
contribution_calibration.why_consequential_not_established: No public source I found poses LS. It is an internal lemma of the dihedral ordered-Olson route. Even combined with S1-sharp it covers only the original LS domain, and gives neither INV*, LS+, STAB nor ordered Olson for D_(2p). There is no matched state-of-the-art quantity to compare against.
contribution_calibration.grouping: G-LS shares one mechanism, and so one priority risk, with the accepted BASE2 cells. LS(17,12) and LS(23,16) lie inside the G-LS domain, so if accepted they should be presented as one contribution.
contribution_calibration.union_with_S1_sharp: This is only a conditional assembly question for the parent: S1-sharp covers κ≤floor(2p/3) for all p≥5, and G-LS covers the rest for p≥7. It is not an accepted theorem and was not evaluated here.
not_established: full LS, LS+, STAB, INV* or ordered Olson

Coverage was web search, arXiv/EJC primary pages and OpenAlex only. No MathSciNet or zbMATH census. OpenAlex's citation count for Lev's arXiv record is 0, which reflects index coverage only.

The [INFERENCE] steps (CRT, the 3p−2 length cap, s_2N(C_p)=2p, η(C_n)=n, GPW⇒Lev, the Dimitrov/Jennings deduction) are elementary deductions of mine, not quoted results. They were not checked by computation.
